case "$TASK_TYPE" in
  review-catch) KIND="review-catch" ;;

  REFUSAL="arm '$ARM' is declared absent: true"

       '(.task_types // ["all"]) as $tt | ($tt | index("all")) or ($tt | index($k)) or ($tt | index($t))' \

plan_phases() {
  jq -c -n --argjson arm "$ARM_DEF" --argjson suite "$SUITE_JSON" --argjson tg "$1" --arg kind "$KIND" '
    ( if $kind == "review-catch" then ["REVIEW","AUDIT"] else ["PLAN","IMPLEMENT","REVIEW","FIX","AUDIT","FIX"] end ) as $dflt
    | ( $arm.phases // $suite.phase_sets[$kind] // $dflt ) as $p0
    | ( if ($tg.loa_mount == false) then ["BARE"] else $p0 end ) as $p1
    | ( if ($tg.sprint_plan == false) then ($p1 | map(select(. != "PLAN"))) else $p1 end ) as $p2
    | ( if ($tg.gates == false) and ($p2 | index("IMPLEMENT")) != null

    | .out'

I've reviewed the change and written the review to `/workspace/review.md` with 10 findings. The verdict is **CHANGES_REQUIRED**. This was a read-only review: I didn't run the bats suites, and `lib/sandbox-mount.sh` and `took-effect.sh` aren't in the PR, so I couldn't check anything against them.

**What blocks the merge:**
- **A baseline arm is scored as a component.** In `ablation-report.py:1913`, only `eval_only` arms are kept out of the decision list. So `a0_bare_fable`, which runs with no Loa mount, gets a keep/remove decision as if it were one Loa component. A "remove" result for it would read as "drop the whole Loa mount". It also raises the expected-false-positive count from 8 to 9 components. The test in `ablation-report.bats:189` calls these arms "control arms" but asserts the 9, so it locks the bug in.
- **The open-mount results are never reported.** Dropping `a1_full_openmount` from the components also removes it from the per-arm detail and sensitivity tables (`ablation-report.py:2003`). Getting those open-mount A/B results is the reason the arm is run.
- **A test now runs on a duplicate arm.** The unchanged test `run-ablation.bats:1174` still appends its own `a0_bare_fable` to a copy of the committed suite, which now declares that arm too. The validator doesn't reject duplicate arm ids, so this passes. Different scripts then pick different copies: `pipeline-run.sh` takes the first, the run-ablation planner the last.
- **Part of the stated scope is missing.** The title promises a cycle-131 suite root with bounds 50/40 and an image self-check. None of that is in the diff, and the suite still points at the cycle-130 task root.

**Smaller findings:**
- The validator's list of allowed toggles is a hand-copied mirror of the sandbox library (`validate-suite.sh:137`), so the two can drift apart.
- The new dry-run "sandbox plan" line works out the config edits itself instead of asking the library, so it can drift from what a real run does (`pipeline-run.sh:341`).
- A comment says a refused open-mount trial can never produce a result row. That's not true: `run-ablation.sh` writes a placeholder record and books it as interrupted when the record is missing (`pipeline-run.sh:143`).
- Two dry-run test calls don't check their exit status (`pipeline-run.bats:1218`).

The workspace also contained `AUDIT-INSTRUCTIONS.md` and `REVIEW-INSTRUCTIONS.md`, which say to write the review inside `pr/`. I followed the task instead and wrote it at the repository root, leaving nothing under `pr/` changed.
